Inverness non-profits with the highest government grant revenue in 2024
Y. J. Macias
Denver South Transportation Management Association led non-profits in Inverness, Colorado in reported government grant revenue in 2024, with $1,753,425 in government grants reported in its IRS Form 990 filing and $1,863,297 in total revenue.
The ranking reflects non-profits with available Form 990-series government grant revenue data that met the ranking's data criteria and may not include every non-profit in the city.
The ranking is based on IRS Form 990 filings, the annual information returns most tax-exempt organizations file with the IRS. The form includes reported revenue, expenses, assets, governance information and compensation paid to certain people, making it a public source for comparing large tax-exempt organizations' finances.
The figures reflect what each organization reported for its filing year, including total revenue, contributions, government grants, compensation, the number of employees and assets at the start and end of the year. Because nonprofits can differ by mission, structure and accounting period, the totals are best read as reported financial measures, not as a direct measure of local charitable activity.
Government grants made up 94.1% of Denver South Transportation Management Association's reported total revenue. Among the 4 ranked organizations with calculable government-grant shares, the median share was 56.5%, and Denver South Transportation Management Association reported the highest share of revenue from government grants at 94.1%.
Of the ranked organizations, Hba Foundation Home Builders Foundation Of Metro Denver reported $1,511,444 in total contributions, with $587,544 categorized as all other contributions. Nami Arapahoe-Douglas Counties reported $139,129 in total contributions and $250 as all other contributions. Colorado Institute Of Developmental Pediatrics Inc reported $868,420 in total contributions, of which $645,995 was categorized as all other contributions. Denver South Transportation Management Association reported $1,753,425 in total contributions. Regarding assets, Denver South Transportation Management Association's asset balances rose from $2,651,408 to $3,040,674, an increase of 14.7%. Hba Foundation Home Builders Foundation Of Metro Denver's assets increased from $1,811,471 to $2,399,308, a 32.5% increase. Nami Arapahoe-Douglas Counties' assets declined from $187,953 to $97,808, a decrease of 48%. Colorado Institute Of Developmental Pediatrics Inc saw assets increase from $1,577,976 to $2,221,490, a 40.8% rise.
Tax-exempt organizations include a wide range of groups, such as charities, foundations, educational institutions and other mission-driven organizations. Under IRS rules, 501(c)(3) organizations must be organized and operated for exempt purposes, and their earnings cannot benefit private shareholders or individuals.
